name: Kestrel Coffee Works
description: A bright corner roastery with a house espresso blend and single-origin pour-overs on a rotating bar. Big communal oak table, fast free wifi, and plenty of outlets, so remote workers camp here all morning. No food beyond pastries from a neighbouring bakery. Dogs welcome on the patio.

name: The Quiet Hour
description: A deliberately laptop-free cafe: no wifi, phones on silent, conversation kept low. Dim lighting, soft jazz, deep armchairs and a small library of secondhand paperbacks. Known for a nutty Brazilian filter coffee and a thick cardamom hot chocolate. Reading, journalling and quiet dates only.

name: Mochi & Milk
description: Japanese-style cafe serving matcha lattes whisked to order, hojicha, and a short menu of mochi doughnuts and fluffy soufflé pancakes. Oat, soy and almond milk at no extra charge. Small, often a queue at weekends, mostly seats of two. Cash-free.

name: Ferrous
description: A minimal concrete-and-steel espresso bar aimed at coffee purists. Competition-grade gear, a rotating guest roaster, and baristas who will talk grind size with you for twenty minutes. Only three seats plus a standing rail, so it is a takeaway spot. No milk alternatives on the espresso flight.

name: Sunbeam Social
description: A family-friendly cafe beside the park with a fenced play corner, high chairs, baby-changing facilities and a kids' menu. Full brunch served until 15:00, including huevos rancheros and buttermilk pancakes. Step-free access throughout and a wide accessible bathroom. Noisy and cheerful.

name: Night Owl Espresso
description: The only late-night coffee in the city, open until 1am for students and shift workers. Cheap bottomless filter, strong cortados, instant-noodle-grade toasties, and long study benches with lamps and power. Gets loud after 22:00 when the bar crowd drifts in.

name: Fig & Thistle
description: A fully plant-based cafe and bakery. Everything vegan, with a dedicated gluten-free prep bench and clear allergen labelling on every item. Famous for a pistachio-rose cake and a smoky mushroom sandwich. Courtyard garden at the back, no reservations, long weekend waits.

name: Cafe Meridiana
description: A classic Italian bar: standing espresso at the counter in the morning, aperitivo and pastries in the evening. Cornetti baked on site, proper cappuccino before 11, and a granita menu in summer. Marble tables, tiled floor, brisk service. Takes cash and card.

name: Loom
description: A large cafe in a converted mill, built for working: three meeting pods bookable by the hour, a silent mezzanine, monitor-height desks and gigabit wifi. Filter coffee refills are free with any food order. Also hosts evening talks and a Thursday knitting group.

name: Tortuga Cold Brew
description: A tiny kiosk on the waterfront specialising in cold brew, nitro on tap, and coffee tonics. Everything is takeaway in compostable cups, with a handful of deckchairs on the boardwalk. Seasonal citrus cold brew in summer. Card only, queue moves fast.

name: Rosehip Tearoom
description: A traditional tearoom doing full afternoon tea on tiered stands, booked two weeks ahead. Forty loose-leaf teas, scones with clotted cream, and a decent decaf. Floral wallpaper, bone china, no laptops by house rule. Good for birthdays and visiting relatives.

name: Basecamp Coffee
description: Opens at 6am for runners and cyclists, with bike racks, a repair stand and a shower pass scheme. Big flat whites, overnight oats, banana bread and a protein-heavy breakfast bowl. Concrete floors, benches, and a wall of race numbers. Fills up at 8am with commuters.

name: Pergola
description: A glasshouse cafe that turns into a natural wine bar after 17:00. Plants everywhere, a long shared table, and a short seasonal menu of small plates. Good for a slow date, with a candlelit terrace. Espresso is secondary here; the coffee stops being made at 18:00.
